title: Slow Cooker White Bean & Potato Soup
description: A simple creamy-feeling soup made from potatoes and white beans without needing heavy cream.
substitutions: Use unpeeled thin-skinned potatoes to save prep time.
Mash some chickpeas instead of white beans if needed.

steps.text: Add everything to the slow cooker.
Cook until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash a little to thicken and serve.

cookSteps.text: Add 4 cups diced potatoes, 2 drained cans white beans, 5 cups broth, 1 diced small onion, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon thyme, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW about 6 hours, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes and beans directly in the slow cooker until the broth thickens slightly. Stir, taste, and add salt if needed.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months. Add a splash of broth when reheating if it thickens.

title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Dill Potatoes & Green Beans
aliases: lemon potato green bean sheet pan
description: A bright, inexpensive vegetable sheet-pan meal or hearty side with lemon and dill.
substitutions: Use broccoli florets instead of green beans.
Use Italian seasoning instead of dill.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1 1/2 pounds potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil, 1 teaspoon dill, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt on a sheet pan.
Toss 12 ounces green beans with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, add them to the pan, and roast 10 minutes more until tender.
Drizzle 1 tablespoon lemon juice over the hot vegetables and toss before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a hot oven, toaster oven, or skillet for best texture.

title: Leftover Mashed Potato Egg Bowls
description: Warm leftover mashed potatoes topped with quick eggs for an easy breakfast-for-dinner rescue meal.
substitutions: Use leftover baked potato flesh mashed with a splash of milk.
Top with chopped cooked vegetables instead of cheese.

cookSteps.text: Warm 2 cups leftover mashed potatoes until steaming, dividing them between 2 bowls.
Cook 4 eggs in a small skillet the way you like them, seasoning with 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Top each bowl with 2 eggs and 1/4 cup shredded cheese if using. Serve hot.

storage: Best assembled fresh. Refrigerate leftover potatoes separately and use within 4 days of their original cooking date.

title: Small-Batch Cinnamon Apple Oat Crisp
description: A little warm apple crisp with a buttery oat topping, sized for a small household.
substitutions: Use quick oats for a softer topping.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Put 2 chopped apples in a small baking dish and toss with 1 tablespoon brown sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon.
Mix 1/2 cup oats, 2 tablespoons flour, 2 tablespoons softened butter, and 1 tablespoon brown sugar until crumbly. Scatter over the apples.
Bake 25 minutes, until the apples are tender and the topping is lightly browned.
Let stand a few minutes before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat briefly in the microwave or oven.
